report.summary: Reviewed the new createAssessmentLabelSourceFactsCheck renderer, its integration in delivery-assessment.ts, the reused labelsIn/createAssessmentLabelCitationCheck parser, and the accompanying tests, within the packet only. I found one reproducible defect in the negative (changes_suggested) path: lines 125-133 group PAGE labels only by file and Form labels only by the parse5 form start offset, without applying the single-id and owner resolution checks that labelsIn already encodes at lines 76-87. A delivered source containing a 'stray' complete label set that is unreachable or in a template-like, duplicate-id or foreign-owner context is therefore reported as a complete group, which forces 'source_disagrees_with_change' and demotes an otherwise valid changes_suggested item to insufficient_evidence. Positive-path reuse, the skip-for-business-checks gate, the sent-HTML completeness checks, and the rendered explanation wording all behaved as described.

findings.title: Negative PAGE/FORM grouping ignores control-association validity, so unreachable label sets force 'source_disagrees_with_change'
findings.evidence: createAssessmentLabelSourceFactsCheck (lines 125-133) accepts every parsed label whose text is required (or, for FORM, whose label.form exists). For PAGE it sets owner = file (line 128) and for FORM it uses the raw start-offset group id (lines 46 and 128). It does not reuse the validation that labelsIn already performs in the links loop at lines 76-87: a for=label whose target doesn't resolve, has duplicate ids, or whose owner form differs has its form deleted, and form-context required labels have absence requested so the parser returns undefined. The check also does not apply textarea ancestor grouping. So a duplicate or unresolvable label becomes a complete 'group'. delivery-assessment.ts line 472 passes the model's status, and lines 475-477 then set the item to insufficient_evidence with reason manual_interpretation. This contradicts the stated contract that such changes become 'unknown' and that no complete group exists when associations are unresolved.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace, based on the supplied parser semantics. Descriptor: 'Contact page source content must label "Mobile" and "E-mail".' Files: index.html = <html><head><title>T</title></head><body><label>Mobile</label><label for="mail">E-mail</label><input id="mail"><input id="mail"></body></html>. In labelsIn, ids.get('mail') === 2, so line 83 deletes label.form for the E-mail label. In the facts scan (PAGE context), owner = file for both labels, so the group contains Mobile and E-mail. Line 132 returns true and the result is {kind:'unknown', reason:'source_disagrees_with_change'}. In delivery-assessment.ts the item becomes insufficient_evidence with 'manual_interpretation'. A follow-up variant: '<label>Mobile</label><label for="missing">E-mail</label>' also yields source_disagrees_with_change instead of treating the for= target as unresolved. The case at tests/assessment-label-source-facts.test.ts lines 47-48 uses a well-formed other form, so it never reaches the cross-form-owner negative path for a PAGE descriptor.
findings.suggestion: Reuse labelsIn(snapshot[file], {context, requiredLabels: labels}) and group only labels whose association is established: for FORM, require label.form, and for PAGE, exclude each label whose for= id did not resolve to a single owner in this file. Alternative: have labelsIn flag unresolved associations and have lines 125-133 skip flagged labels, or return unknown unresolved_parse_or_owner when a required text appears only on such a label. Then the matching group is only counted when the label is a real, resolvable active label.

limitations: Read-only static review of the supplied packet; no files were executed, no tests or typecheck were run, and no runtime, browser, provider or parse5 behavior was observed.

Files outside the packet (static-resources.ts staticFileKind, source-literal-directive.ts quotedSourceLabelValues, static-markup-directive.ts, parse5 version, requirement-coverage.ts validateSavedCoverage) were not supplied. I assumed staticFileKind's 'html' kind matches the .html extension used at line 167 and that observed coverage is a faithful view of the sent HTML; I could not verify either.
tests/fixtures/qualified-answers-three-replay.json (referenced at tests line 98) was not supplied, so the claimed regression expectations could not be checked against it.

No new sealed Google source or corpus was supplied, consistent with the packet. The assessment targets only the new facts renderer and its call site, not wider semantic-parser expansion, optional risk v4, or acceptance/payment flows.

The finding targets a source that contains an invalid-association decoy label alongside a genuine partial delivery. Whether graders intended such decoys as 'active labels' is a product decision, but the check's own contract states that unresolved required form owner/association should yield unknown, not source_disagrees_with_change.
